title: The number you call at 2am
subtitle: What an advisor is for is rarely visible until the day the plan comes apart.

text: Nothing goes wrong on a good day. That is the whole difficulty.
sub: Most of a booking is quiet admin. The value sits in the small share of trips that go sideways, and you cannot know in advance which one is yours.

title: What it looks like when it breaks

items.head: A flight cancels the night before
items.body: Rebooking, and a call to the line to flag embarkation so your cabin is not quietly released.

items.head: A port is dropped at sea
items.body: Excursions cancelled, refunds chased, a new plan for the day before you have had breakfast.

items.head: Something medical ashore
items.body: The port agent's number, the insurer's claim line, and someone awake in your own time zone.

items.head: The cabin is wrong on arrival
items.body: Moved by someone who knows whom to ask on the ship, rather than by standing in a queue.

quote: The difference between a good trip and a memorable one usually comes down to time.

points.label: 11pm
points.value: Your flight is cancelled. You text me before you have reached the airline desk.

points.label: 11:20pm
points.value: The line is called, embarkation flagged, so the cabin is held rather than released.

points.label: Before dawn
points.value: New routing booked, transfer moved, a hotel found for the night nobody planned.

points.label: Morning
points.value: You board. Nobody at the terminal knows anything went wrong at all.

text: You are not buying a booking. You are buying someone answering.
sub: The fare is identical either way. What differs is whether there is a person with your file already open when the plan comes apart at an inconvenient hour.

title: Send this to the person you'd travel with
body: Then write to me with where you are leaning, and I'll come back with a short list worth your time - and one number that answers.
